original_record.question: The diagram shows a triangle $J K L$ where two lines are drawn from each of the vertices $J$ and $K$ to points on the opposite sides. This divides the triangle into nine nonoverlapping sections. If instead, eight lines are drawn to the opposite sides, four from $J$ and four from $K$, how many nonoverlapping sections would the triangle be divided into? <image1>
original_record.solution: The four lines from $J$ cut the triangle into five sections. Each of the four lines from $K$ cuts five sections, thus creating an extra five sections. Altogether there are $5+4 \times 5(=25)$ sections.  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-073.jpg?height=251&width=460&top_left_y=1805&top_left_x=1318)
